commit_note: This record binds to source_commit 8793fe4d, which is also the lint_correction_commit. scope: Two bounded Linux amd64 delegation-location recipes over the T42.H2e admitted external-tool observations: ObserveExecutionGitExecPathManifest structurally censuses the directory a closed git --exec-path probe reports and binds its core helper to an explicitly selected native Git image, and ObserveExecutionGoSDKLocation binds the GOROOT/GOTOOLDIR pair a closed go env probe reports to an explicitly selected native Go image. Both share one new bounded Linux census layer rather than each reimplementing a directory walk. Neither observation is admitted on Darwin. This slice supplies no launcher authority, no session teardown, no dispatch admission, no Linux input-custody immutability model, no pressure/allocation/restore adapter, no Linux plan version, no resource admission, no freeze, ceremony or scale claim.

census_contract.shared_layer: readExternalDelegationRows performs one refuse-don't-truncate ReadDir batch loop per directory, in batches of 128 entries, and censusExternalDelegationRoot wraps it with an explicit entry bound.
census_contract.identity_fence: The directory identity is snapshotted before the first read and re-checked after the last against both the open handle and the path, so a concurrent replacement or resize cannot supply the observed rows.
census_contract.entry_name_rules: A name that is empty, "." or "..", longer than maxInputCustodyPathBytes, or containing NUL, CR or LF is refused.
census_contract.sort_requirement: Rows are sorted explicitly with slices.SortFunc over strings.Compare because (*os.File).ReadDir returns kernel directory order rather than a sorted sequence, and every downstream digest depends on that ordering.
census_contract.over_bound_behavior: A directory that exceeds its entry bound refuses outright; the census never emits a digest describing a prefix of an unadmitted shape.
classes_refused: any entry carrying a setuid or setgid bit
census_contract.symlink_recording: A symlink contributes its target alone, capped at maxExternalDelegationSymlinkBytes, because its size and permission bits are kernel conventions rather than delegated structure.
census_contract.header_screen: A regular helper's own class comes from externalDelegationHelperClass, which reads at most maxExternalDelegationHeaderBytes through the existing non-following t4013.OpenHostImage and separates \x7fELF native from #! script from sourced text. It never executes, loads, vendor-validates or reads a helper body.
census_contract.canonical_encoding: externalDelegationCanonical encodes each sorted row as its class, a space, then the length-prefixed fields name, helper, size, perm and target, then a newline. Prefixing each field with its own byte length makes the digest input injective, so a hostile entry name cannot resplit a row.
census_contract.observation_carries: No absolute host path, no entry name and no entry content. The assertion is not vacuous by collision: it forbids real entry names of this host's exec-path and GOROOT (mergetools, git-remote-http, VERSION, gofmt, preprofile) against the %#v encoding, each verified present on the host first.
census_contract.bounds_rationale: Directory bounds are entry counts rather than byte counts because the shape being proved is structural; the two byte bounds that matter, 64 MiB per helper and 64 MiB per subdirectory, are enforced from Lstat sizes without opening a body. The measured host shapes sit inside every bound with headroom: 172 exec-path root entries against 512, one subdirectory against four, 24 mergetools entries against 128, 16 GOROOT root entries against 64, 2 bin entries against 8 and 8 tool entries against 64.
census_contract.git_oracle: The manifest requires exactly one regular native git entry that hashes byte-equal to the selected image, plus at least one symlink whose target map names git, so neither a directory of unrelated helpers nor a lone copied core satisfies the recipe. Every symlink must name a bare sibling - not ".", not "..", not itself, and not a path carrying a separator - that is itself an admitted regular helper in the same census, so a link that escapes the directory, points at a directory or chains to another link refuses. At most four subdirectories are admitted, each as a flat non-empty collection of bounded regular files totalling at most 64 MiB. The census re-checks that NativeHelpers+ScriptHelpers+TextHelpers == RegularFiles+SubdirectoryEntries before it will emit a digest.
census_contract.go_oracle: The recipe binds the reported pair rather than either field alone: GOTOOLDIR must equal exactly GOROOT/pkg/tool/<goos>_<goarch>, GOROOT/bin/go must resolve back to the admitted image and hash byte-equal to it, and both the on-disk VERSION marker's first line and the image's own go version output must equal runtime.Version(), so the recorded release never reaches a caller through a path that skipped that check. The root census admits regular files and real directories only and requires the five directory markers api, bin, lib, pkg and src plus the two non-empty regular markers VERSION and go.env; bin must hold exactly the two native executables go and gofmt; the tool directory must be a non-empty flat set of native executables and is digested without reading a single tool body.
census_contract.go_census_precedence: The bin census and its exact-pair admission run before the bin/go digest, which is the precedence the Git recipe already keeps between its census and its core-image digest, so an oversized or otherwise unadmitted bin entry is refused on its metadata alone and no body of it is read.
census_contract.in_sdk_reads: Exactly three reads reach inside the SDK, and they differ by purpose rather than by size: the VERSION marker is the only read of SDK content for that content's own sake, bounded at 4,096 bytes; the shared census layer reads at most 64 header bytes per regular entry purely to classify it; and censusExternalGoSDKLocation fully reads GOROOT/bin/go once to bind the SDK to the admitted image. None of the three walks the tree around it.
census_contract.closed_environment: Both recipes run under the existing externalToolEnvironment, which sets neither GIT_EXEC_PATH nor GOROOT, so a hostile ambient value cannot reach either census. Every refusal case is therefore produced by calling the unexported censuses directly on synthetic fixture directories rather than by poisoning an environment.
census_contract.validPublicToolVersion_exception: validPublicToolVersion deliberately does not apply to the path-valued probe output, because it is a location rather than a version; go version output is instead compared by strict exact equality.
census_contract.named_result_convention: Both observers accumulate into a local and assign their named result only at the single success return, so a refusal yields the zero value rather than a partial description of an unadmitted shape. The shared layer keeps that convention at its own two boundaries: a refused probe zeroes its named output even when its deferred cleanup also failed, and every classification refusal returns an explicit zero entry, so a refused row's name or symlink target cannot travel past the error that rejected it.
census_contract.descriptor_bound: Each census holds at most one directory descriptor plus one header-read descriptor at a time and closes both with checked errors, and os.OpenRoot containment means no entry name is ever concatenated into an escaping path.
census_contract.platform_fence: Both stay Linux-amd64-only behind a //go:build linux file and a runtime.GOARCH != "amd64" refusal, issue no CheckoutAdmissionBinding, add no field to ExecutionToolIdentity, and leave validateExecutionHost as the separate freeze-platform fence, so an observed identity remains neither a launch recipe nor dispatch authority.

cost_pass.steady_state: No new per-query/request, sync tick, startup/restart, retry/no-op or publication work; ordinary runtime is unchanged and no production dispatch site is added or removed. Neither observer is called from any production path, so both cost nothing until a future ceremony entry point wires them, and each is bounded by construction rather than by a deadline on a subprocess.
cost_pass.git_observation: One 30-second outer context, one image admission (EvalSymlinks, one full hash of the 4,547,768-byte core image and one ELF64 header screen), one --exec-path child under the existing ten-second probe context with its 4-KiB stdout and stderr caps, one private scratch directory, and one bounded census of at most 512 root entries plus at most four subdirectories of at most 128 entries each. On this host that measured 196 census rows, 145 Readlink calls, 50 header reads of at most 64 bytes each, and five full reads of the one core image for 22,738,840 bytes hashed. No other helper body is read at all, and the 31,571 bytes of mergetools content contribute only their Lstat sizes.
cost_pass.go_observation: The same outer context and image admission over the 15,434,568-byte bin/go, two children, and 26 census rows with 18 header reads, at most 4,096 bytes of the one VERSION marker (35 bytes measured) and two source-marker directory admissions. It hashes that single path in full at each of its verification points, for 108,041,976 bytes across seven reads: admission, before and after each of the two probes, the GOROOT/bin/go equality read and the final re-verification. The SDK is never walked, so its measured 15,026 files across 1,667 directories and 232,413,581 bytes stay entirely outside every bound, and no tool body is read.
cost_pass.rejected_on_cost: Content-hashing all 172 exec-path entries, which would read 26 helper bodies plus 24 text files for no version-probe value, and a GOROOT tree digest through the existing hostTreeDigest, which would turn one location recipe into a 232,413,581-byte scan.
cost_pass.held_resources: Each census holds at most one directory descriptor plus one header-read descriptor at a time and closes both with checked errors. No new persistent lock, cache, timer, goroutine, store/schema, corpus/shard, publication or disk work. Probe scratch is removed by the existing deferred cleanup unless a volume-owned preparation parent deliberately retains it, which is the retained T42.H2e behaviour and is asserted unchanged by TestExternalProbePreparationParentRetainsScratch.

low_findings: censusExternalGoSDKLocation digested GOROOT/bin/go before the bin census, so that path was hashed in full before maxExternalDelegationHelperBytes bounded its row; the Git recipe already kept the safer precedence. Corrected by running the bin census and admitExternalGoSDKBin ahead of the digest, with the precedence and its consequence stated in the census comment. The only changed expectation is bin_go_is_absent, which now reaches the exact-pair fence before the digest fence; the digest fence stays covered by bin_go_differs_from_the_admitted_image.

runExternalDelegationProbe joined a cleanup failure into retErr but left its named output populated, so a refused probe could hand partial output to a caller beside a non-nil error. The defer now zeroes output whenever retErr is non-nil, matching the observers' own convention.

classifyExternalDelegationRow returned a partially filled entry carrying the refused row's name and symlink target alongside its error. All four refusal paths now return an explicit zero entry, and the function comment records why.

Both census tests took their expected digests from the production externalDelegationDigest, which made the assertion tautological against a change to the "sha256:" prefix or the hash function. Each fixture now also carries one independently computed hard-coded hex digest, asserted equal to externalDelegationDigest of the hand-written canonical string before use.

Both new test files asserted refusals with strings.Contains, weaker than the exact-equality precedent in external_delegation_linux_test.go. Every refusal assertion in the two new tables, the SDK directory-admission table and its bin_go_is_absent subtest now compares err.Error() to the complete production message, so a fence reordering that lets one rule refuse where another was expected fails instead of passing on a shared prefix.

The two RefusesUnadmittedImages tables asserted only that a refusal occurred. Each gains a want field pinning the exact message for all eight cases, derived from the production guard order: the platform and context guards, then the absolute-path, resolution and native-image screens, then the single generic probe refusal that catches a real native image of the wrong role.

The real-host assertions forbade only private directories, so a bare leaked entry name was unpinned outside the synthetic tests. They now forbid names that are real entries of this host's exec-path and GOROOT (mergetools, git-remote-http; VERSION, gofmt, preprofile), each verified present on the host and each checked against the %#v encoding so the assertion is not vacuous by collision.
